mainTopic: תשמיש as עינוי, washing and anointing on יום כיפור, crossing water for a מצוה, and the future river from the קדש הקדשים
overview: The גמרא finishes proving that holding back marital relations is called עינוי. It reads לבן's warning to יעקב, 'אם תענה... ואם תקח', as two separate things and defends that reading against two challenges. רב פפא then asks how this fits the story of שכם, where the act itself is called עינוי. אביי answers that שכם's עינוי was unnatural relations. Next, a ברייתא teaches that on יום כיפור washing or anointing even part of the body is forbidden, unless it is done to remove dirt or as medicine. A mother may rinse one hand to feed her child, and the חכמים made שמאי הזקן feed his children with two hands. The גמרא then lists cases where a person may walk through water on יום כיפור: to greet a father or teacher, to guard fruit, to come to a שיעור, or to ask a halacha, as long as he does not lift his robe. רב יוסף asks whether such deep water may be crossed even on a weekday, based on the river in יחזקאל, and אביי answers that a fast-flowing river is different. The amud ends with teachings about that future river flowing from the קדש הקדשים: no swimmer, no boat, and not even the מלאך המות can cross it. A spring that starts tiny widens as it flows out, and a supporting משנה begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading לבן's warning as two separate things
steps.stepSummary: 'אם תענה' refers to holding back marital relations; 'ואם תקח' refers to bringing in rival wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If you shall afflict' my daughters means by holding back marital relations. 'And if you shall take' other wives means causing them pain through rival wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two halves of לבן's warning to יעקב. It assigns each half its own meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the proof that holding back relations is called עינוי. Since 'ואם תקח' already covers rival wives, 'אם תענה' must mean something else, and that is holding back relations. This is useful for the larger question of what counts as עינוי on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: 'If you shall afflict' — by holding back marital relations,
'and if you shall take' — through rival wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation earlier that תשמיש is called עינוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In לבן's warning, 'תענה' means holding back relations and 'תקח' means rival wives.

steps.title: Maybe both halves are about rival wives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both 'תענה' and 'תקח' could be talking about צרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that this phrase and that phrase are both about rival wives?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just gave. It suggests both halves of the verse might mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both halves are about צרות, then 'תענה' has nothing to do with holding back relations. The whole proof would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: this one and that one, both of them

phrases.english: But say that this one and that one are both about rival wives?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'אם תענה' refers to holding back relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both phrases could describe the same pain of rival wives, so the verse would not prove that holding back relations is called עינוי.

steps.title: The extra 'and' shows a new topic
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'ואם תקח' with a ו, which signals a separate idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'if you shall take'? It is written 'and if you shall take'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the exact wording of the verse. The added 'and' (ו) shows the second half adds something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both halves were about rival wives, the verse would not need 'and' to join them as two items. 'ואם' tells us these are two different kinds of suffering, so 'תענה' must mean something other than צרות.

keyTerms.meaning: is it written…? (asking about exact wording)

phrases.english: Is it written 'if you shall take'?
'And if you shall take' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the verse describe rival wives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו in 'ואם' shows a second, different topic, so 'תענה' is not about rival wives.

steps.title: Maybe the two halves are two kinds of rival wives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests one half refers to wives יעקב already has and the other to new wives from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both are about rival wives: one about his own rivals (the maidservants he already has), and one about rivals who would come to him from the outside world, which fits 'if you shall take'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to make both halves about צרות. This time it accepts that the ו means two items, but says they are two different kinds of rival wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This new version answers step 3. 'תענה' would mean raising the maidservants בלהה and זלפה, who are already in the house, to full wife status. 'תקח' would mean marrying new women from outside. This keeps two separate items without any reference to holding back relations.

phrases.english: But say that both are about rival wives,
one about his own rivals,
phrases.notes: The maidservants already in his house (בלהה and זלפה)

phrases.english: and one about rivals who come to him from the outside world,
which fits 'if you shall take'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מִצָּרוֹת, חַד לְצָרוֹת דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger version of the challenge in step 2. It gets around the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that 'תענה' must mean holding back relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separate items can both be about rival wives (existing ones and new ones), so the ו does not prove that 'תענה' means holding back relations.

steps.title: The order of the verse does not fit
steps.stepSummary: If both halves were about rival wives, the verse should have said 'תקח' first and 'תענה' second, but it says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'if you shall take and if you shall afflict'? It is written 'if you shall afflict and if you shall take'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the order of the words in the verse. That order does not fit the suggestion of two kinds of rival wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both halves were about rivals, the natural style would build up: 'don't take new wives, and don't even raise up the maidservants' (תקח, then תענה). The verse puts תענה first, so it is not part of that build-up. It must be a separate topic, holding back relations, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'not only this, but even this', a build-up style of speaking

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer is just 'the words are in a different order'. The point is that the build-up a listener would expect when both parts are about rival wives would put 'take' first. Since the verse does not follow that build-up, 'afflict' must be a different subject.
steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'אם תענה את בנותי' stands as the source that holding back marital relations is called עינוי. Both attempts to read it as only about rival wives were answered: first from the ו, then from the order of the words.

phrases.english: Is it written 'if you shall take and if you shall afflict'?
'If you shall afflict and if you shall take' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the order of the words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תענה' means raising the maidservants and 'תקח' means new wives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order of the verse does not fit that reading, so 'תענה' means holding back relations.

steps.title: רב פפא: relations themselves are called affliction
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that in the story of שכם, the act of relations itself is called עינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But relations themselves are called affliction, as it is written: 'And he lay with her and afflicted her'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the whole idea with a different verse. If the act itself is called עינוי, how can holding it back also be called עינוי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about שכם and דינה seems to use עינוי for having relations. That looks like the opposite of what we just proved, that holding back relations is the עינוי.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But relations themselves are called affliction,
as it is written: 'And he lay with her and afflicted her'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the conclusion of steps 1-5, using a different verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that holding back relations is called עינוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah calls the act itself עינוי, so it seems odd that holding it back would also be called עינוי.

steps.title: אביי: שכם's act was unnatural relations
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that שכם's עינוי was relations done in an unnatural way, which is real suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, he afflicted her through unnatural relations.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא. The verse about שכם is about a special, painful kind of relations, not normal relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal marital relations are a pleasure, so holding them back is עינוי. In the case of שכם, the עינוי was that he used her in an unnatural way, which caused real pain. So the two verses do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
he afflicted her through unnatural relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's קשיא in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The act of relations itself is called עינוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only unnatural relations are called עינוי. Normal relations are a pleasure, and holding them back is עינוי.

steps.title: Washing part of the body on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that washing even part of the body is forbidden, but someone who is dirty may wash normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: It is forbidden to wash part of one's body just as it is forbidden to wash the whole body. But if he was dirty with mud or excrement, he washes in his usual way and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the details of the ban on washing (רחיצה) on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not only on a full bath. Washing even one part of the body for pleasure is also forbidden. When a person washes only to remove dirt, it is not for pleasure, so it is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic halacha of יום הכפורים: the ban covers even part of the body, but washing to remove dirt, which is not for pleasure, is allowed.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לִרְחוֹץ מִקְצָת גּוּפוֹ כְּכׇל גּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: It is forbidden to wash part of one's body just like the whole body,
but if he was dirty with mud or excrement —
he washes in his usual way and need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָסוּר לִרְחוֹץ מִקְצָת גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the details of washing on יום הכפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing even part of the body is forbidden, but washing off dirt or excrement is allowed.

steps.title: Anointing part of the body on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא teaches that anointing even part of the body is forbidden, but a sick person or someone with scalp sores may anoint normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden to anoint part of one's body just as it is forbidden to anoint the whole body. But if he was sick, or had sores on his head, he anoints in his usual way and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the ban on anointing (סיכה) on יום הכפורים. It follows the same pattern as washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like washing, anointing even one part of the body is forbidden. When the oil is used as medicine or to ease the pain of sores, it is not for pleasure, so it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום הכפורים, both washing and anointing are forbidden even for part of the body. They are allowed when done to remove dirt or as medicine, not for pleasure.

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לָסוּךְ מִקְצָת גּוּפוֹ כְּכׇל גּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: It is forbidden to anoint part of one's body just like the whole body,
but if he was sick,
or he had sores on his head —
he anoints in his usual way and need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָסוּר לָסוּךְ מִקְצָת גּוּפוֹ כְּכׇל גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, applying its pattern to anointing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anointing even part of the body is forbidden, but a sick person or someone with scalp sores may anoint.

steps.title: A woman may rinse one hand to give bread to her child
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a woman may rinse one hand in water on יום כיפור so she can give bread to her child.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of מנשה taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a woman may rinse one hand in water, give bread to the child, and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. A small amount of washing is allowed on יום כיפור so that a mother can feed her child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that washing even part of the body is forbidden on יום כיפור. This teaching adds a case where it is allowed: rinsing one hand so the child can eat. The rinse is not done for pleasure. It is done for the child's needs, so it is not the forbidden kind of washing.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of מנשה taught
And she need not be concerned

phrases.english: The school of Menashe taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A woman may rinse one hand in water,
and give bread to the child,
phrases.notes: This way she does not touch the bread with an unwashed hand.

phrases.english: and she need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: She is not violating the ban on washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another permitted case of washing, after the exceptions in Steps 8-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may rinse one hand on יום כיפור in order to give bread to her child.

steps.title: שמאי הזקן is overruled and told to feed with two hands
steps.stepSummary: שמאי הזקן was strict and would not feed with even one hand. The חכמים decreed that he must feed with two hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about שמאי הזקן that he did not want to feed with one hand, and they decreed on him to feed with two hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about שמאי הזקן, who refused to wash even one hand to feed his children. The חכמים forced him to be lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי went beyond the leniency of the previous step and would not wash even one hand. The חכמים did not just permit one hand. They required him to feed with both hands, so his strictness would not leave the children without food. This shows that being extra strict here is wrong when it causes children to suffer.
steps.confusionAlert: שמאי was not being lenient. He was being too strict by refusing to wash even one hand. The decree pushed him toward leniency.

phrases.english: They said about Shammai the Elder
that he did not want to feed with one hand,
phrases.notes: He did not want to wash even one hand on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and they decreed upon him to feed with two hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that strengthens the leniency of Step 10 by showing the חכמים rejecting extra strictness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים required שמאי to feed his children with two hands rather than avoid washing.

steps.title: Why do the hands need washing at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for washing the hands before touching the child's food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. Why is washing needed before giving food?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last two steps assumed that hands must be washed before handling food, even on יום כיפור. The גמרא now asks what makes unwashed hands a problem.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the washing allowed in Steps 10-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the hands must be washed before touching food.

steps.title: אביי: because of the evil spirit שיבתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that unwashed hands carry a harmful spirit called שיבתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: because of שיבתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Washing is needed because of a harmful spirit called שיבתא that rests on unwashed hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unwashed hands in the morning carry שיבתא, which can harm the food and the child who eats it. Because there is real danger, rinsing the hand counts as a need and not a pleasure. This explains why the washing is allowed on יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: An evil spirit that rests on unwashed hands

steps.whatToRemember: Washing to remove danger (שיבתא) is permitted on יום כיפור, because it is not washing for pleasure.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Because of Shivta.
phrases.notes: A harmful spirit on unwashed hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unwashed hands carry the harmful spirit שיבתא, so they must be rinsed before touching food.

steps.title: Crossing water to greet one's father or teacher
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows someone going to greet his father, teacher, or a greater person to cross water up to his neck on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one who goes to greet his father, his teacher, or someone greater than him may cross water up to his neck and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Entering water for a מצוה purpose, such as honoring one's father or teacher, is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking through water is like bathing, which is forbidden on יום כיפור. Still, when a person goes to honor someone, he may cross even deep water. The purpose is the מצוה, not pleasure, so it is not forbidden washing.

keyTerms.meaning: To greet (to receive the face of)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who goes to greet his father
or his teacher,
or one who is greater than him —
may cross up to his neck in water
and need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַהוֹלֵךְ לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case of permitted contact with water on יום כיפור, this time for a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One going to greet his father, teacher, or a greater person may cross water up to his neck on יום כיפור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that entering water for a מצוה is not the forbidden bathing of יום כיפור.

steps.title: May a teacher cross water to visit his student?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the same leniency applies when a teacher goes to his student.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about a teacher going to a student?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the ברייתא. The ברייתא only spoke of going to someone greater, so what about a teacher going to his student?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's cases all involve honoring someone greater. When a teacher goes to his student, he is not giving honor, but he may be going to teach Torah. The question is whether this purpose is also strong enough to permit crossing water.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A teacher going to a student

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
A teacher going to a student — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הָרַב אֵצֶל תַּלְמִיד מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the leniency of Step 14 extends to the reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a teacher may cross water on יום כיפור to go to his student.

steps.title: Proof: זעירי crossed to his student
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר בר חנה reports seeing זעירי go to his student רב חייא בר אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יצחק בר בר חנה said, I saw זעירי, who went to רב חייא בר אשי, his student.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a story. A great teacher, זעירי, went through water to his student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If זעירי, the teacher, crossed water to reach his student, then a teacher may do so. The proof depends on the story being told correctly, with the teacher going to the student.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: as Rav Yitzḥak bar bar Ḥana said:
I saw Ze'iri

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲזַל לְגַבֵּי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי תַּלְמִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: who went to Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi, his student.
phrases.notes: He crossed water on יום כיפור to reach him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the question of Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a teacher may cross water to go to his student.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The eyewitness report of רב יצחק בר בר חנה about זעירי.

steps.title: רב אשי: actually the student went to the teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the story was reversed: רב חייא בר אשי went to his teacher זעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: in that case, it was רב חייא בר אשי who went to זעירי, his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the proof. He says the facts were the opposite, so the story proves nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the student went to the teacher, the story only repeats the ברייתא's case of going to one's teacher. It tells us nothing about a teacher going to a student, so the question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of a teacher crossing water to his student is left unresolved, because the זעירי story is disputed.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי הוּא
phrases.english: In that case, it was Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi
who went to Ze'iri, his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָהוּא רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the factual basis of the story, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was reversed. The student went to the teacher, which the ברייתא already permits.

steps.title: רבא allows fruit guards to cross water
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits the people on the far side of the river to walk through water on יום כיפור to guard their fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא allowed the people living across the river to pass through the water to guard the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical ruling of רבא: people who must guard their fields across the water may walk through it on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking through water normally looks like the forbidden bathing of יום כיפור. רבא treats guarding one's crops as a real need, so getting wet on the way does not count as forbidden bathing.

keyTerms.meaning: the far (right) side of the river

phrases.english: Rava permitted the people of the right side of the river
to pass through the water
to guard the fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case where crossing water on יום כיפור is allowed, this time for protecting property instead of honoring a teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit guards may walk through water on יום כיפור to reach and guard their crops.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא that supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבא that a ברייתא says the same thing: fruit guards may cross water up to their necks without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: a ברייתא supports you. Guards of fruit may cross through water up to their necks, and they need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up רבא's ruling with an earlier source that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבא's ruling is not just his own idea; it is an established teaching. It even allows water up to the neck, which is the same depth as the ruling in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: and they need not be concerned

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
A baraita was taught that supports you:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמְרֵי פֵּׂירוֹת עוֹבְרִין עַד צַוָּארָן בְּמַיִם
phrases.english: Guards of fruit cross in water up to their necks
and they need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that fruit guards may cross water on יום כיפור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: fruit guards may cross water up to their necks without concern.

steps.title: רב יוסף lets people come to his lecture but not go home
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף permits the people of בי תרבו to cross water to come to his שיעור, but not to cross back home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף allowed the people of בי תרבו to cross through the water to come to the lecture. He did not allow them to go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another ruling: crossing water to come to learn Torah is allowed, but going home is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming to the שיעור is a מצוה, so it justifies crossing. Going home is just a personal trip, so רב יוסף did not see it as a good enough reason.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף שְׁרָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי בֵּי תַרְבּוּ
phrases.english: Rav Yosef permitted the people of Bei Tarbu
to cross in the water to come to the lecture;
to go back, he did not permit them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף שְׁרָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי בֵּי תַרְבּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case of crossing water, now for learning Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crossing water to come to a שיעור is allowed; crossing back home is not.

steps.title: אביי: forbidding the return will stop them from coming
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that if people cannot go home, they will not come to the שיעור in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, you are making them stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's ruling by pointing to its practical result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people know they will be stuck on the far side after the שיעור, they simply will not come next time. So forbidding the return trip ends up damaging the מצוה of coming.

keyTerms.meaning: you make them stumble / you hold them back

steps.confusionAlert: Here לעתיד לבא does not mean עולם הבא. It just means 'next time, in the future.'

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן אַתָּה מַכְשִׁילָן לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.
phrases.english: If so, you are obstructing them in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן אַתָּה מַכְשִׁילָן לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the restriction in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ban on crossing back home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Banning the return trip will stop people from coming at all, so it defeats the מצוה the leniency was meant to help.

steps.title: Second version: רב יוסף allowed both coming and going
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רב יוסף allowed them both to come and to go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he allowed them to come and allowed them to go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the story. This sets up a new question from אביי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version there is no restriction at all. Now the question is turned around: why is going home allowed?

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁרָא לְהוּ לְמֵיתֵי וּשְׁרָא לְהוּ לְמֵיזַל,
phrases.english: he permitted them to come and permitted them to go,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שְׁרָא לְהוּ לְמֵיתֵי וּשְׁרָא לְהוּ לְמֵיזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate account of step 20's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crossing water is allowed both to come to the שיעור and to return home.

steps.title: אביי asks why going home is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי understands allowing them to come, but asks for the reason to allow them to go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Coming makes sense, that's fine. But going back, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רב יוסף to explain the leniency for the trip home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming is for a מצוה, so it is clear. Going home seems to be only a personal need, so אביי wants the reason.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Granted, to come — well and good,
but to go, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמֵיתֵי — לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא לְמֵיזַל מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second half of step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for allowing the trip home through the water.

steps.title: Allowing the return keeps people coming
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that going home is allowed so that people will not be held back from coming in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you will not make them stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the return trip is allowed to protect the מצוה of coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same idea אביי used as a challenge in the first version is the answer in the second version. The trip home is allowed because it is tied to the trip to the שיעור.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, אביי objects to forbidding the trip home. In the second, רב יוסף himself allows it. Either way, the reasoning is the same: forbidding the return would discourage people from coming to the שיעור in the future.

phrases.english: So that you will not obstruct them
in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא מַכְשִׁילָן לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The return is allowed so people will not be discouraged from coming to the שיעור in the future.

steps.title: רמי בר פפא calls across the river with a question
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה stand on one riverbank; רמי בר פפא, on the other side, calls out asking whether he may cross to ask them a halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה were standing on the bank of the river פפא at the crossing of חצדד, and רמי בר פפא was standing on the other side. He called out to them: May I cross to come to you to ask a halacha?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story and sets up a question: may one cross water on יום כיפור to go ask a halachic question?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is like coming to a שיעור, but for a personal question instead of a public lecture. The answer will come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: on the bank of the river

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda and Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda
were standing on the bank of the Pappa River
at the crossing of Ḥatzdad,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה קָאֵי רָמֵי בַּר פָּפָּא מֵהָךְ גִּיסָא.
phrases.english: and Rami bar Pappa was standing on the other side.
He raised his voice to them:
May one cross to come to you
to ask a halakha?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ לְמִיעְבַּר לְמֵיתֵי לְגַבַּיְיכוּ לְמִשְׁאַל שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story extending the idea of crossing for Torah study.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may cross water on יום כיפור to go ask a halachic question.

steps.title: רב יהודה: you may cross, but keep your hand down
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers in the name of רב and שמואל: one may cross, as long as he does not lift his hand out from under the hem of his robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: רב and שמואל both say: One may cross, as long as he does not take his hand out from under the hem of his robe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה allows the crossing, but adds a condition about how to cross.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crossing itself is allowed for Torah learning. The condition is that he must not lift his robe up to keep it dry, because carrying it that way counts as forbidden carrying on יום כיפור, just as on שבת. He must walk normally and let his clothes get wet.
steps.confusionAlert: The condition is not about how deep the water is. It is about not lifting the clothing up, which could count as carrying.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to him:
Rav and Shmuel both say: one may cross,
provided that he does not take out his hand
from under the hem of his cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר פפא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, he may cross, but he must not lift his robe out of the water.

steps.title: Second version: רב שמואל בר רב יהודה answers from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רב שמואל בר רב יהודה answered, quoting the same rule from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב שמואל בר רב יהודה said to him: We learned in a ברייתא: One may cross, as long as he does not take his hand out from under the hem of his robe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of who answered and where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is the same in both versions. The only difference is the speaker and the source: a statement of the אמוראים רב and שמואל, or an older ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: one may cross water on יום כיפור to ask a halacha, but must not lift his robe.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda said to him:
We learned: one may cross,
provided that he does not take out his hand
from under the hem of his cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate version of the answer in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Same ruling, attributed to a ברייתא and said by רב שמואל בר רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even on a weekday, deep water seems forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: is it even allowed on a weekday to walk through water this deep? He starts a step-by-step reading of the פסוקים in יחזקאל. The first stage permits crossing water up to the ankles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Is it even allowed on a weekday to cross like this? But it is written: 'He measured a thousand אמות and led me through the water, ankle-deep water.' From here we learn that one may cross water up to the ankles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the whole idea of crossing deep water, asking whether it is even allowed on a normal weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue now is not bathing on יום כיפור but danger. רב יוסף reads each stage of יחזקאל's river as a permitted depth, starting with the ankles. In the next step the stages continue up to the waist, and beyond that the river is one that 'cannot be crossed.' אביי answers the challenge in step 30.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the discussion from a יום כיפור question (bathing) to a general safety question (danger of drowning), which affects every crossing discussed so far.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחוֹל כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: And on a weekday, is it permitted in such a way?
But isn't it written: "He measured a thousand cubits
and he led me through the water, water to the ankles" —
from here, that one is permitted to cross up to the ankles.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וּבְחוֹל כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leniency of crossing deep water given in steps 26-27 (and the earlier rulings).
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to cross deep water, such as water up to the neck.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים in יחזקאל permit crossing only up to the waist (step 29), because deeper water is dangerous. So how can neck-deep crossing be allowed on יום כיפור if it is not even allowed on a weekday?

steps.title: Water may come up to the knees and the waist, but no higher
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his challenge from the פסוקים. Knee-deep and waist-deep water may be crossed, but beyond the waist the verse calls it a river that cannot be crossed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He measured a thousand and led me through water up to the knees.' From here we learn that one may cross water up to the knees. 'He measured a thousand and led me through water up to the waist.' From here we learn that one may cross water up to the waist. Beyond that: 'He measured a thousand, a river that I could not cross!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues the challenge he began in step 28. He walks through the פסוקים in יחזקאל to show that crossing water deeper than the waist is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each measured stage of the river becomes a rule: ankles, then knees, then waist are all allowed. Once the water goes past the waist, the פסוק says the prophet could not cross. So how could רמי בר פפא cross a river that deep, even on a weekday?

keyTerms.meaning: From this point on, beyond this

phrases.english: "He measured a thousand and led me through the water,
water up to the knees" —
from here we learn that one may cross water up to the knees.
"He measured a thousand and led me through water up to the waist" —
from here we learn that one may cross water up to the waist.
Beyond that:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיָּמׇד אֶלֶף נַחַל אֲשֶׁר לֹא אוּכַל לַעֲבוֹר״!
phrases.english: "He measured a thousand, a river that I could not cross"!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל מז:ה. This implies that deeper water is dangerous and may not be crossed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא begun in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 26 that רמי בר פפא may cross a deep river
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים allow crossing only up to the waist. Water deeper than that is 'a river I could not cross,' so such a crossing should be forbidden even on a weekday.

steps.title: A fast-flowing river is a special case
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the river in the פסוק is different because its water rushes along.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A river is different, because its water flows fast.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's challenge. The danger in the פסוק comes from rushing water, not simply from deep water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'waist limit' only applies to a strong, fast current, where a person could be swept away. Still water deeper than the waist is not covered by this limit. So the original ruling for רמי בר פפא can stand.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A river is different, because its water flows fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 28 and 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (fast current versus still water)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any water above the waist may never be crossed
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fast-flowing water above the waist is too dangerous to cross. Still water may be crossed.
steps.whatToRemember: The waist-limit from יחזקאל applies to rushing rivers, not to still water. That is how the ruling for רמי בר פפא survives.

steps.title: The future river cannot be crossed by swimming
steps.stepSummary: Turning to the river in יחזקאל itself, the גמרא says one might think the prophet could swim across, but the פסוק says 'מי שחו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he could cross it by swimming. Therefore the verse says: 'For the water had risen, water of שחו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new topic. It explains more of the description of the future river, starting with whether one could swim across.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'יכול... תלמוד לומר' pattern: suggest a possibility, then use a פסוק to rule it out. Swimming is the first option to be eliminated. The meaning of 'מי שחו' is explained in the next steps.

phrases.english: One might think he could cross it by swimming —
therefore the verse says:
"For the water had risen, water of שחו."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halacha back to the river in יחזקאל itself and explains more of its description
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The future river cannot be crossed by swimming

steps.title: What does 'מי שחו' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase 'מי שחו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'מי שחו'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unusual phrase 'מי שחו' means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof against swimming depends on this phrase. If we do not know what 'שחו' means, we cannot tell how it rules out swimming.

phrases.english: What is "מי שחו"? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in the proof of step 31

steps.title: 'מי שחו' means water that needs a boat
steps.stepSummary: 'מי שחו' means water that can only be crossed by boat, because sailing is sometimes called 'swimming.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It means sailing, since people call sailing 'swimming.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'שחו' refers to sailing. This is water too deep to swim through, so you would need a boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In everyday speech, the word for swimming (סייחא) was also used for sailing (שייטא). So 'מי שחו' means 'water you would have to sail across,' which rules out swimming. This raises the next question: could a boat cross it?

phrases.english: It means sailing,
for people call sailing 'swimming.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מי שחו' means water that can only be crossed by boat, not by swimming

steps.title: A small boat cannot cross it either
steps.stepSummary: One might think a small boat could cross, but the פסוק in ישעיה says 'בל תלך בו אני שיט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he could cross it in a small boat. Therefore the verse says: 'No rowing boat shall go on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the next option: a small boat. It brings a פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'מי שחו' suggested the river needs a boat, we might think a small boat would work. The פסוק 'אני שיט' (a rowing boat) says no.

keyTerms.meaning: A rowing boat, galley with oars

phrases.english: One might think he could cross it in a small boat —
therefore the verse says:
"No rowing boat shall go on it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 33: if the water needs a boat, the גמרא checks whether a small boat would do
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small boat cannot cross the future river

steps.title: Even a large ship cannot cross it
steps.stepSummary: One might think a large ship could cross, but the פסוק says 'וצי אדיר לא יעברנו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he could cross it in a large boat. Therefore the verse says: 'And a mighty ship shall not pass over it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the last option, a large ship, using the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the פסוק in ישעיה rules out a different kind of boat. The end result is that nothing can get across this river.

phrases.english: One might think he could cross it in a large boat —
therefore the verse says:
"And a mighty ship shall not pass over it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves up from a small boat to a large one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a large ship cannot cross the future river

steps.title: How do we know which phrase means which boat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that these words in the פסוק refer to a small boat and a large boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the פסוק's words mean a small boat and a large ship. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אני שיט' and 'צי אדיר' are unusual. The proofs in steps 34 and 35 only work if those words really mean a small boat and a large ship.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this implied? Where do we see this?

phrases.english: How is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis behind how steps 34 and 35 read the פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that 'אני שיט' and 'צי אדיר' mean a small boat and a large ship

steps.title: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's תרגום reads the פסוק as 'a fishing boat will not go on it, and a large ship will not cross it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translated it: A fishing boat will not go on it, and a large ship will not cross it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף translates 'אני שיט' as a fishing boat, which is a small boat. He translates 'צי אדיר' as 'בורני רבתי,' a large ship. This confirms how steps 34 and 35 read the פסוק.

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates:
A fishing boat will not go on it,
phrases.notes: Translation of 'בל תלך בו אני שיט'

phrases.english: and a large ship will not cross it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף's תרגום shows that the פסוק refers to a small fishing boat and a large ship
steps.whatToRemember: The future river cannot be crossed in any way: not by swimming, not by a small boat, and not by a large ship.

steps.title: Even the מלאך המות cannot cross the river
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן פזי teaches that even the מלאך המות may not pass through the river. He learns this from the shared word 'שיט' / 'שוט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן פזי said: Even the מלאך המות has no permission to pass through it. It is written here: 'No rowing boat (שיט) shall go on it,' and it is written there: 'From roaming (שוט) the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן פזי adds that even the מלאך המות cannot cross this river. He proves it by linking a word in ישעיה to the same word in איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איוב, the שטן (who is also the מלאך המות) says he comes 'from roaming (שוט) the earth.' The same root appears in 'אני שיט' about the river. So the פסוק that blocks the 'שיט' also blocks the one who does 'שוט,' meaning the מלאך המות cannot cross.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (a word-link between פסוקים)
From roaming, going to and fro

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about boats. It works only through the shared root שוט/שיט, which links the river to the שטן's 'roaming' in איוב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת אֵין לוֹ רְשׁוּת
phrases.english: Even the Angel of Death has no permission
to pass through it,

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״בַּל תֵּלֶךְ בּוֹ אֳנִי שַׁיִט״,
phrases.english: it is written here: "No rowing boat (shayit) shall go on it,"

steps.title: The spring grows wider as it flows outward
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס, quoting רב הונא צפוראה, describes the spring that comes out of the קדש הקדשים. It starts as thin as a grasshopper's antenna and gets wider at each stage: the פתח ההיכל, the אולם, and the פתח העזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס said in the name of רב הונא צפוראה: The spring that comes out of the קדש הקדשים starts out as thin as a grasshopper's antennae. When it reaches the entrance of the היכל, it becomes as thick as a warp thread. When it reaches the אולם, it becomes as thick as a woof thread. When it reaches the entrance of the עזרה, it becomes as wide as the mouth of a small jug.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the future river. This teaching describes how the river starts tiny inside the קדש הקדשים and gets wider as it moves outward through the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this one talked about how great the river will be once it is fully grown. This teaching goes back to the very beginning and traces the river's growth one stage at a time. Each stage of the building (היכל, then אולם, then עזרה) matches a slightly wider size, so the river grows on its own as it travels.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש
Grasshoppers' antennae, used here as a picture of something extremely thin
Warp and woof, the two sets of threads in weaving; the woof thread is thicker than the warp thread
The entrance hall in front of the היכל

steps.confusionAlert: The order runs from the inside out: קדש הקדשים, then היכל, then אולם, then עזרה. The river gets wider as it moves away from the holiest place, not narrower.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס מִשּׁוּם רַב הוּנָא צִפּוֹרָאָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rav Huna of Tzippori:
The spring that comes out from inside the Holy of Holies,
at first resembles grasshoppers' antennae (very thin);
once it reaches the entrance of the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: The היכל is the main hall just outside the קדש הקדשים.

phrases.english: it becomes like a warp thread;
once it reaches the Entrance Hall,
it becomes like a woof thread (thicker);
once it reaches the entrance of the Courtyard,
it becomes like the mouth of a small jug.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס מִשּׁוּם רַב הוּנָא צִפּוֹרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new aggadic teaching about the same future river, this time tracing how it grows from its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spring from the קדש הקדשים starts as thin as a grasshopper's antennae and widens in stages until it is as wide as the mouth of a small jug at the entrance of the עזרה.

steps.title: A משנה supports this description
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a משנה from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to show that this picture of the spring is already found there. The quotation begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: Water...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to quote a משנה that matches רבי פנחס's teaching, but the quote only begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase והיינו דתנן means 'this is the same thing that a משנה teaches.' It shows that the teaching from רב הונא צפוראה has an older source in a משנה. The detail that the water is like 'the mouth of a small jug' will turn out to be the link between the two sources.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what we learned in a משנה,' a phrase that ties a teaching to a matching משנה
The תנא whose משנה is about to be quoted

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: Water...
